newsitem.title: USA: New CBOE chairman says tax issue a priority.
newsitem.headline: New CBOE chairman says tax issue a priority.

text.p: Bill Brodsky, the new chairman of the Chicago Board Options Exchange, said Thursday that resolving a longstanding taxation issue was one of his first major tasks.

"One of the top initiatives in the coming period of my tenure is to work with the leadership of the industry to deal with a provision in the federal tax code, which is called the short-short rule," Brodsky told a luncheon of the Investment Analysts Society of Chicago.
The short-short rule affects mutual funds holding investments for less than 90 days.

It changes the funds' pass-through status for short-term capital gains tax when short-term gains exceed 30 percent of their profit. It can pose a problem for options users, who could have their buy-write positions called away.
Brodsky said proposals to amend the short-short rule had not been able to pass Congress because they had been tied up in an omnibus tax bill.
"What we've got to do is find a way to get this passed," he said.
He told Reuters that introducing a separate bill to specifically address the issue was one option. He declined to say which legislators the CBOE would be working with.
Another major undertaking in the early part of Brodsky's chairmanship would be the migration next month of the New York Stock Exchange's options business, which CBOE has purchased.
"We're building a trading hall for the New York Stock Exchange traders with all the technology we have available," Brodsky said.
Some 50 NYSE market-makers trading options on about 200 stocks will start trading in Chicago on April 28.
Brodsky has said he would be picking up where outgoing chairman Alger "Duke" Chapman left off, noting that CBOE was in very good shape both operationally and financially.
He said he would continue to foster investor education programs and technological enhancements.
With 70 percent of all orders coming onto the floor electronically, CBOE was already among the most technologically advanced exchanges, he said.
Brodsky, previously president of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, officially took over the helms at CBOE on March 10 from Chapman, who retires from CBOE posts as of end-March.
